thread:
incident-bot: INCIDENT PAGE — High KV/prefix cache miss rate for enterprise VPC tenant 'nimbus-corp' (dedicated pool dp-37). Severity: P1. Alert: prefix_hit_rate < 10% for 5m, tail latency spikes > 2s. Paging oncall-sre-1.

oncall-sre-1: ACK — seeing large spike in 95th token latency from dp-37, CPU on proxy nodes high, KV cache miss ratio jumped. tagging marco-eng + emily-sre.

marco-eng: I can join. quick ask: is this isolated to nimbus-corp or hitting multiple tenants?

emily-sre: Metrics show dp-37 tenant namespace (tenant:nimbus-) prefix_hit_rate = 7.2% (baseline ~78%). Other tenants on same pool at ~70-90%. Looks like namespace collision / pollution. Logs show frequent evictions from the tenant's prefix bucket.

oncall-sre-1: +1. Looks like their prefix keys are extremely high-cardinality (per convo with cs). Could be tail of requests that bypass cache or a bug in prefix hashing.

sarah-cs: Hi folks — customer (Bob) reports requests timing out in their integration tests and production ingest backpressure. They are seeing ~5-10x cost increase because of regen. Bob (customer-nimbus-bob) is in thread.

jordan-ops: grabbing live state:
```
kubectl get pods -n dp-37 -o wide
NAME                                     READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
kv-cache-agent-0                         2/2     Running   0          12d
kv-cache-agent-1                         1/2     Running   0          12d
proxy-pool-37-5fcd9                      3/3     Running   0          8d
```
metric snapshot (past 10m):
prefix_hit_rate{tenant="nimbus"} = 0.072
prefix_evictions{tenant="nimbus"} = 12456
kv_backend_latency_p50 = 18ms, p95 = 2.1s
```

nate-ml: Paging note — fallback models are available but customer requires response parity. If we route to fallback it may change quality. Prefer to fix cache asap.

marco-eng: Quick mitigation plan: 1) isolate tenant namespace to dedicated cache partition (if available) OR 2) temporarily disable prefix caching for tenant to stop pollution and reduce evictions, 3) throttle client's write-heavy prefixes, 4) apply a more aggressive TTL for their prefixes.

oncall-sre-1: Which is fastest? We can flip a tenant-level flag to disable prefix caching in ~2min, or trigger namespace isolate which requires a rolling restart of cache agents (~10-12min).

emily-sre: If we disable prefix caching for nimbus, hit rate will drop to 0 for prefixes but avoids thrashing other tenants and should reduce p95 on the pool. CPU and evictions should drop. Risk: increased backend calls for repeated prefixes — but given current miss rate it's already happening.

sarah-cs: Customer asks for ETA and expects minimal quality change. They prefer non-invasive if it keeps throughput.

oncall-sre-1: I'll do the tenant-level prefix_cache=false toggle now. Notifying customer.

oncall-sre-1: /run ops-toggle --tenant nimbus --prefix-cache false --reason "incident: hit-rate collapse"

incident-bot: command accepted, executing..

jordan-ops: change applied to cp-config for tenant:nimbus -> prefix_cache=false, propagated to kv-cache-agent via config-poller.

(2m later)
emily-sre: Observability update: prefix_hit_rate metric for nimbus is now 'N/A' (disabled). Overall dp-37 pool evictions down 83%, p95 backend latency dropped from 2.1s -> 420ms, token tail latency for customer reduced ~60%.

customer-nimbus-bob: Thanks — we see responses returning and fewer timeouts. Still seeing some slow tails but much better. Appreciate the communication.

nate-ml: Note: model fallback not used. No model-level changes. Good.

marco-eng: Next steps while we keep prefix caching disabled for nimbus: 1) run a scan of their prefix key distribution to find hot ranges and dedupe; 2) create a dedicated namespace/partition for dp-37 if pattern continues; 3) patch prefix hashing to reduce collision risk. I'll open a PR for telemetry to expose per-namespace cardinality.

oncall-sre-1: Handoff to emily for monitoring and follow-up. emily, please own until we revert or create partition.

emily-sre: Ack. I'll keep an eye on evictions, cpu, and tail latency and run the forensic job (kv-prefix-scan --tenant nimbus) now. Output will be uploaded to incident channel.

emily-sre: KV prefix scan output (summary): total unique prefixes: 3.2M, top-100 prefixes account for 2.3% of requests, very long tail of single-use prefixes — likely user-generated request ids in the prefix.

marco-eng: That aligns: high-cardinality prefixes -> cache pollution. Proposed medium-term mitigation: namespace isolation for nimbus and a small policy change to ignore user-generated id fields from prefix key building (sanitize prompts/keys).

sarah-cs: Customer asks for timeline for isolation.

marco-eng: Estimate 10-20min to create and migrate tenant to isolated cache partition with a controlled rolling restart of two agents (no model restarts). We'll schedule a low-impact migration window and coordinate with customer.

oncall-sre-1: For now we'll keep prefix caching disabled and monitor for 1 hour. If stable, we plan migration in off-peak.

customer-nimbus-bob: Please keep me informed. We need an RCA and an ETA for re-enable.

emily-sre: Logged incident ticket INC-2026-1849, attaching metric dumps and scan. Will produce initial RCA draft within 24h.

jordan-ops: ops note: revert command if needed -> /run ops-toggle --tenant nimbus --prefix-cache true --reason "re-enable after mitigation"

oncall-sre-1: Thank you all. Marking this thread as ongoing mitigation. I'll reassign to emily for monitoring and mark incident-bot with update. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: UPDATE — mitigation applied (tenant-level prefix cache disabled). Severity downgraded to P2 for observation window.

last message emily-sre: 40m check-in: metrics stable, evictions low, customer reports normal ops. Plan: schedule namespace isolation tomorrow, implement sanitization PR this week, postmortem with customer and internal blameless RCA.
